The fourteenth beta of CoSky 8.0, still for developers to try. It fixes the low-severity problems the review of the whole project found, in every part: the server, the Redis store, the client, the Spring Boot starter, `cosky-migrate` and the Dashboard. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

There is no compatibility promise before `8.0.0-rc.1`, which freezes what [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning) lists.

## Try it

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes: a server in development mode, a Spring Boot application that reads a Config and registers, and another that finds it.

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0-beta.14 --dev
```

What helps most is still what we could only try on one machine: Redis Sentinel or Cluster of your own with a failover, an OIDC provider other than Keycloak, moving a 6.x installation with `cosky-migrate`, and a real network. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you.

## Fixed

### Server and Redis store

- **A namespace deleted just as a replica found a fork kept its data.** Replacing the epoch did not look at whether the namespace was being deleted, and the deletion, which goes by the epoch, then removed nothing. Only an active namespace's epoch is replaced now. (#1299)
- **A namespace deleted and created again within a second could give out a lease id again,** and deleting one could leave a lease behind when a renewal came in between. The lease sequence now stays with the namespace's revision when it is deleted, and the leases go first. (#1297, #1299)
- **Anti-entropy could take a reload for drift,** and replace the epoch for nothing: every watcher of the namespace then read it anew, at the time it was busiest. (#1297)
- **A long but healthy reaper round counted as an outage,** with thousands of namespaces or a slow network to Redis, and dead instances stayed well past their lease. (#1297)
- **A Config import was applied in part, and did not say which part.** The whole archive is checked before anything is written, and one that fails halfway names what it wrote. (#1297)
- **The topology of every namespace stopped refreshing when one could not be recorded,** as with a Redis Cluster shard down. (#1297)
- **Followers waited for their next poll after the Redis subscription came back,** for the writes made while it was down. (#1297)
- **A watch that ended could take a newer watch of the same id with it,** for clients that reuse watch ids, which then went on out of reach of Cancel and of a change of permissions. (#1297)

### Client and Spring Boot starter

- **A lease shorter than about 11 seconds was reaped before a silent renewal stream was noticed.** (#1295)
- **A watch started over could keep instances that were gone,** from a chunk of the stream before. (#1295)
- **While a required Config was deleted, no other import refreshed.** The application now keeps what that Config held, logs a warning, and goes on refreshing the rest. (#1295)
- **A refresh that added the first `cosky:` import made a second client,** which nothing closed and nothing refreshed for. (#1295)
- **An application that failed late in its start left its client open.** (#1295)

### `cosky-migrate`

- **Running it again with another `--default-format` left the format as it was** for Configs named without an extension. It now changes the format of those it imported and nobody edited on 8.0, and lists them in the report. (#1296)
- **A proxy or login page answering in place of the server was reported as "Cannot write the report".** The run now stops saying what came back, and the report is written. (#1296)

### Dashboard

- **Deleting went ahead whatever had changed since the row was read,** such as tokens added to a ServiceAccount. It now sends the row's revision. (#1298)
- **What was read right after one's own save could be older than the save,** from a replica that was behind. (#1298)
- **After a failover, pages without live updates waited for a revision of the old timeline,** and every read timed out until the page was reloaded. (#1298)
- **A token created from Connect application was lost if the drawer closed first,** and **a token offered in a notice stayed after signing out.** (#1298)

### API

- **A request with many invalid fields reached gRPC clients as a transport error,** past the 8 KiB of trailers they accept by default. The error now lists the first violations, and how many more there are. (#1296)

## Upgrading from beta.13

- Nothing changes: the gRPC API, the protos, REST, the data in Redis and the properties. Applications stay on Spring Boot 4.2.0 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.0. `cosky-migrate` and the Dashboard come with this release.
- Replicas of beta.13 and beta.14 can run side by side during a rolling upgrade.
- An `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with many violations lists those that fit, and ends with "and N more".
- A required Config deleted while the application runs is now a warning in its log, not a failed refresh.
- beta.13 reached GitHub Packages only in part (`cosky-api`, `cosky-client` and `cosky-bom`), and its `cosky-migrate` zip was attached by hand afterwards. Use Maven Central for it, or this release.

## Known limits

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **On Sentinel,** while a master that hangs still holds the connection hints come on, each replica reads every namespace every second instead. A write then takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 30% of its CPU. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **A late Namespace creation that takes a write before it is undone** stays, without an object, and the server logs an error. That takes a write in the round trip between making the namespace and dropping it.
- **Removing every CoSky import at once** leaves their properties in place. A refresh that loaded no CoSky Config at all is not taken as one that ran the imports, so that nothing is dropped by mistake.
- **The server does not stop an account from granting itself roles** it may write; see the security guide.
